gloss: smelling of the sea; having a briny, seaweed-like odor

definitions.gloss: smelling of the sea; having a briny, fishy, or seaweed-like odor
definitions.explanation: Describing the characteristic smell of a rocky seashore — a mix of salt water, seaweed, and marine life. Can be either evocative (nostalgia for the coast) or unpleasant depending on context.

examples.japanese: {港|みなと}の{近|ちか}くは{磯臭|いそくさ}い。
examples.english: It smells briny near the harbor.

examples.japanese: {磯臭|いそくさ}い{風|かぜ}が{吹|ふ}いてきた。
{海|うみ}から{上|あ}がると{体|からだ}が{磯臭|いそくさ}くなるので、すぐシャワーを{浴|あ}びた。
examples.english: After getting out of the sea my body smelled briny, so I took a shower right away.

notes:
A compound adjective from {磯|いそ} (rocky shore, seashore) + {臭|くさ}い (smelling of, -smelling). The {磯|いそ} specifically refers to rocky coastline as opposed to sandy beaches, so the smell is associated with seaweed, tide pools, and exposed marine life.

USAGE:
The word can be neutral or slightly negative. For some it evokes pleasant seaside memories; for others it describes an unwanted fishy smell. The suffix ～{臭|くさ}い is productive in Japanese: {汗臭|あせくさ}い (sweaty-smelling), {酒臭|さけくさ}い (reeking of alcohol), etc.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {磯臭|いそくさ}い{風|かぜ} — sea-scented wind
- {磯臭|いそくさ}い{匂|にお}い — briny smell
- {磯|いそ}の{香|かお}り — scent of the shore (more poetic/positive)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {生臭|なまぐさ}い — smelling of raw fish, fishy (stronger; more unpleasant)
- {潮|しお}の{香|かお}り — scent of the sea breeze (poetic; always positive)
- {魚臭|さかなくさ}い — smelling of fish (specifically fish, not the general shore smell)

forms.label: Conditional たら
forms.negative: {磯臭|いそくさ}くなかったら
